annotations.annotation_text: Page 380 opens Book 2, Chapter 3 ("The Tavern") during the Age of Heroes phase. This passage continues HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging, featuring HCE, the Twelve Customers, Butt and Taff. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "Liffey" on page 380 ("The Tavern"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. In this Age of Heroes passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.

The Age of Heroes dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
